exercise.title: Major and minor chords: one note apart
exercise.why: A major and a minor chord on the same root share the root and the 5th, so the 3rd is the only note you have to listen for.

cells.text: Tap {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} on the staff below: a major chord on {{=key}}, one note at a time.

Now tap {{1}} {{b3}} {{5}} on this staff: the minor chord on the same root. Only the 3rd moved, down a half step.
Go back and forth between the two staffs. Practice until you can tell the two chords apart with your eyes closed.
{{?key}}In another key the notes are new, and the two chords still differ by that one note.

Press Play below to start the backing track: {{chord:I}} and {{chord:i}}, the two chords you just built, each lasting one, two or three bars. Look away from the chord boxes and say major or minor each time the chord changes, then look back to check.
If you lose your place, wait for the next change and start again from there.
